panels.title: Overall Health Score
panels.description: Single 0-100% roll-up of system health, taken from the system:health_score:percentage recording rule. 100% means nothing is wrong. Check that rule's definition for exactly what counts against the score.

panels.title: Active Alerts by Severity
panels.description: Alerts currently firing as critical or warning, plus pending ones (condition is true but hasn't yet lasted the rule's 'for' duration). Anything above zero deserves a look; the Active Alerts table below shows which ones.

panels.title: Failed Units
panels.description: Number of systemd units currently in the failed state. Should be 0. The 'Systemd Failed Units' graph further down shows which units; investigate with systemctl status <unit> and journalctl -u <unit>.

panels.title: Hottest Sensor
panels.description: Highest temperature reported by any hwmon sensor (CPU, board, drives) right now. Sustained high readings usually point to cooling problems or throttling; see 'Temperature Sensors' for the per-sensor breakdown.

panels.title: System Uptime
panels.description: Time since the last boot. A low value you weren't expecting means an unplanned reboot, crash or power loss.

panels.title: Kernel
panels.description: Kernel release currently running (from node_uname_info). If it differs from the newest installed generation after an upgrade, a reboot is still pending.

panels.title: Root Filesystem Usage
panels.description: Percent of the root (/) filesystem in use, calculated from free bytes. Free bytes include space reserved for root, so the space actually usable by normal users can be slightly less than this shows.

panels.title: RAM Usage
panels.description: Percent of RAM not available to applications (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). Reclaimable cache counts as available, so a high value here means genuine memory pressure rather than just a full page cache.

panels.title: Swap Usage
panels.description: Percent of swap space in use. Some swap use is normal for cold pages; sustained high use together with Memory Pressure or Memory Paging Activity means the machine is short on RAM.

panels.title: 🔔 Active Alerts (firing + pending) — with rule condition
panels.description: Built from the ALERTS metric. 'condition' is the PromQL expression and 'for' duration that triggered the alert (added automatically by withCondition in maintenance-alerts.nix). Use a cell's inspect icon to read long values; click an alertname to open it in Prometheus.

panels.title: Firing by Category
panels.description: Count of firing alerts grouped by their 'category' label (for example os), from the system:alerts_by_category:count recording rule. Shows which area of the system is unhealthy.

panels.title: Firing by Checklist Section
panels.description: Count of firing alerts grouped by their 'checklist_section' label (for example II.6), from the system:alerts_by_section:count recording rule. Maps alerts back to the matching section of the maintenance checklist.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Average CPU busy percentage across all cores over the last 5 minutes (100 - idle). I/O wait is not counted as idle here, so a machine stalled on disk can show high usage while doing very little real work.

panels.title: CPU Usage Over Time
panels.description: Average CPU busy percentage across all cores over time (100 - idle, 5m rate). I/O wait counts as busy here, so compare with IO Pressure when usage looks high but nothing is actually working hard.

panels.title: CPU Load Average
panels.description: Load average divided by core count for 1, 5 and 15 minute windows. 1.0 means every core is occupied on average; sustained values above 1 mean tasks are queuing. On Linux, load also counts tasks stuck waiting on disk, so a failing or stalled drive can raise load without raising CPU use.

panels.title: CPU Pressure
panels.description: Pressure Stall Information (PSI): share of time at least some tasks were waiting for CPU time. Rising values mean CPU contention even if overall usage looks fine.

panels.title: Memory Pressure
panels.description: Pressure Stall Information (PSI) for memory. 'Some processes waiting' = at least one task was stalled on memory; 'All processes blocked' = every non-idle task was stalled. Sustained non-zero 'all blocked' means the machine is thrashing.

panels.title: Memory Usage Breakdown
panels.description: Stacked view of RAM: applications (Used), buffers, cache (page cache plus reclaimable slab) and free. Cache is handed back on demand, so a small Free slice is normal; a growing 'Used (apps)' slice is what to watch.

panels.title: Swap Usage
panels.description: Swap used and free over time. Steady growth suggests a memory leak or too little RAM. Use together with Memory Paging Activity to tell whether swap is actively being read and written or just holding cold pages.

panels.title: Disk Space Usage
panels.description: Percent used for each real mounted filesystem. Virtual filesystems (tmpfs, overlay, squashfs and similar) and the /nix/store and /run mounts are excluded. See 'Estimated Time Until Disk Full' for the trend.

panels.title: Inode Usage
panels.description: Percent of inodes used per filesystem (same exclusions as Disk Space Usage). A filesystem can be unable to create files while still showing free space if it runs out of inodes, which happens with millions of small files.

panels.title: Disk IO Operations
panels.description: Completed read and write operations per second for each block device (5m rate). A high count is only a problem if the disk is also saturated or slow; compare with Disk Utilization and Disk IO Latency.

panels.title: Disk Utilization (busy %)
panels.description: Share of time each device had I/O in flight (like iostat %util). Near 100% on a spinning disk means it is saturated; on SSD/NVMe the number is less meaningful because they service requests in parallel. Low utilization alongside high I/O wait or IO Pressure suggests stuck or very slow I/O rather than heavy load.

panels.title: Estimated Time Until Disk Full (current 6h trend)
panels.description: Projection based on how free space has changed over the last 6 hours, extrapolated linearly. Only filesystems whose free space is shrinking appear. Red < 1 day, orange < 1 week. A one-off large write can make it look more urgent than it is.

panels.title: IO Pressure
panels.description: Pressure Stall Information (PSI) for disk I/O. 'Some processes waiting' = at least one task was stalled on I/O; 'All processes blocked' = every non-idle task was stalled. Measures the impact on the workload, so it catches slow or stuck devices that utilization numbers can miss.

panels.title: Network In
panels.description: Total inbound traffic across physical network interfaces (loopback, veth, docker and bridge devices excluded), 5 minute average.

panels.title: Network Out
panels.description: Total outbound traffic across physical network interfaces (loopback, veth, docker and bridge devices excluded), 5 minute average.

panels.title: Network Traffic
panels.description: Inbound (rx) and outbound (tx) throughput for each physical network interface, 5 minute average. Loopback, veth, docker and bridge devices are excluded.

panels.title: Temperature Sensors
panels.description: Every hwmon temperature sensor (CPU cores, motherboard, drives and so on), labelled by sensor and chip. Look for sustained high readings or sudden jumps.

panels.title: CPU Frequency (min / avg / max)
panels.description: Minimum, average and maximum current clock speed across cores, compared with the rated maximum. CPUThrottling fires when cores run below 60% of rated max under load. Low frequency at idle is normal power saving; low frequency under load suggests thermal or power throttling.

panels.title: Clock Offset
panels.description: Difference between the system clock and its time reference (node_timex_offset_seconds). ClockDrift fires above 0.1 s for 10 min. Large offsets cause TLS, authentication and log-correlation problems.

panels.title: Systemd Failed Units
panels.description: One line per systemd unit currently in the failed state (value 1). An empty graph means every unit is healthy. Investigate with systemctl status <unit> and journalctl -u <unit>.

panels.title: Service Uptime History
panels.description: Whether each scrape target was reachable over time (the 'up' metric: 1 = scraped successfully, 0 = down or unreachable). The prometheus and node jobs are excluded.

panels.title: Alert Counts Over Time
panels.description: Number of alerts firing over time, split by severity. Shows whether problems are brief blips or persistent, and when they started.

panels.title: Alert Timeline (what fired, when)
panels.description: One row per alert name showing when it was firing over the selected time range. Useful for correlating alerts: which fired together, and which came first.

panels.title: Scrape Targets
panels.description: Every Prometheus scrape target and whether it could be reached (up: 1 = yes, 0 = no).

panels.title: Scrape Duration
panels.description: Longest scrape time per job. Slow scrapes are an early sign of an overloaded exporter or network problem, and scrapes that approach the scrape timeout will start failing.

panels.title: TSDB Head Series
panels.description: Number of active time series held in Prometheus's in-memory head block. Memory use scales with this; a sudden jump usually means a label cardinality explosion.

panels.title: TSDB Size on Disk
panels.description: Disk space used by Prometheus's persisted data blocks (the write-ahead log is not included). Grows until the retention limit starts removing old blocks.

panels.title: Rule Eval Failures (1h)
panels.description: Rule evaluations that errored in the last hour. Non-zero means an alert or recording rule is erroring and silently not firing; check the Prometheus Rules page or logs for the failing rule.

panels.title: Slowest Rule Group
panels.description: Duration of the most recent evaluation of the slowest rule group. If it approaches the group's evaluation interval, evaluations can be delayed or skipped and alerts may lag.

panels.title: Container CPU (% of one core)
panels.description: CPU used by each container, as a percentage of a single core (200% = two cores fully used), 5 minute average.

panels.title: Container Memory
panels.description: Working-set memory per container: memory actively in use, excluding easily reclaimable cache.

panels.title: Memory vs Limit
panels.description: Working-set memory as a percentage of each container's memory limit. Containers with no limit are omitted. Matches the ContainerHighMemory alert (90%).

panels.title: Restarts (24h)
panels.description: How many times each container has started in the last 24 hours, detected from changes in its start time. Repeated non-zero values point to crash loops or out-of-memory kills.

panels.title: Traefik Requests by Status Code
panels.description: Requests per second handled by Traefik, stacked by HTTP status code. Watch for growth in 4xx (client or routing problems) and 5xx (backend failures).

panels.title: Traefik 5xx Ratio by Service
panels.description: Fraction of each service's requests that returned a 5xx error (0.05 = 5%). HighHTTPErrorRate fires above 5%.

panels.title: Probe Status
panels.description: Result of each blackbox probe over time (probe_success): success or failure per target. A failing band means the endpoint was unreachable or failed its check.

panels.title: ICMP Latency
panels.description: Ping round-trip time to each target, measured by the blackbox exporter. HighNetworkLatency fires above 100 ms.

panels.title: Time Since Last Successful Backup

defaults.noValue: no backup metrics (needs the custom backup exporter)

panels.description: How long since each backup job last completed successfully. BackupJobFailed fires after 24 h.

panels.title: Backup Size
panels.description: Size of each backup job's most recent output over time. BackupSizeAnomaly fires on a >30% change vs last week; a sudden drop can mean missing data, a spike unexpected growth.

panels.title: Certificate Time Remaining
panels.description: Time until each probed TLS certificate expires. Orange under 30 days, red under 7.

panels.description: Quarterly maintenance checklist: tasks to work through each quarter. Tick them off as you go and log completion in the Maintenance row.

panels.title: Per-Core CPU Usage
panels.description: Busy percentage for each individual core (100 - idle, so I/O wait counts as busy). Reveals single-threaded bottlenecks that the all-core average hides.

panels.title: Context Switches & Interrupts
panels.description: System-wide rate of context switches and hardware interrupts. Sudden sustained spikes can point to a runaway process or a misbehaving driver or device.

panels.title: Disk IO Bandwidth
panels.description: Bytes read from and written to each block device per second (5m rate).

panels.title: Disk IO Latency (await)
panels.description: Average time per completed read or write over 5 minutes, per device. Spinning disks are typically in the milliseconds, SSDs well under 1 ms. Rising latency with little throughput suggests a failing or contended device. Gaps mean no I/O happened in the window.

panels.title: Network Errors & Drops
panels.description: Packet errors and drops per second, receive and transmit, per interface. Should sit at zero; persistent non-zero values point to cable, driver or buffer problems.

panels.title: TCP Connections by State
panels.description: Established TCP connections, sockets in TIME_WAIT, and total allocated TCP sockets. Large TIME_WAIT counts mean many short-lived connections; allocated sockets approaching system limits can cause connection failures.

panels.title: Memory Paging Activity
panels.description: Rates from /proc/vmstat: 'Pages In/Out' (pgpgin/pgpgout) count data moved to and from disk in KiB per second; 'Swap In/Out' count memory pages swapped per second. Sustained swap activity means the machine is short on RAM.

panels.title: File Descriptors
panels.description: System-wide open file handles allocated versus the kernel maximum. If allocated approaches maximum, processes start failing with 'too many open files'.

panels.title: SMART status (1 = healthy)
panels.description: Each drive's overall SMART self-assessment (1 = PASSED). PASSED only means no attribute has crossed its failure threshold: a drive can pass while accumulating reallocated or pending sectors, so also check the raw SMART attributes.

panels.title: Drive temperature
panels.description: Temperature each drive reports via SMART. Spinning disks generally prefer to stay below about 50 °C; SSDs tolerate more but may throttle when hot.

panels.title: NVMe wear (percent of endurance used)
panels.description: Percentage of the NVMe drive's rated write endurance already consumed (from the drive's own counter). 100% means the rated lifetime has been reached; plan replacement well before that.

panels.title: Time since each timer last fired
panels.description: How long since each listed systemd timer (nixos-upgrade, flake-update, backup-home, nixlab-gpull, nix-gc) last triggered. A value far beyond the timer's schedule means it is stuck, disabled or failing to run.

panels.title: Journal errors by unit
panels.description: Journal entries at error severity or worse (err, crit, alert, emerg), counted per systemd unit in each graph interval. Spikes identify the noisy or failing service.

panels.title: Failed SSH logins
panels.description: Failed password and invalid-user attempts logged by sshd, per host and graph interval. Bursts indicate brute-force scans; consider fail2ban or limiting SSH exposure.

panels.title: Kernel warnings
panels.description: Kernel log lines matching error, fail or warn (case-insensitive). The place to spot disk I/O errors, hardware faults, driver crashes and NFS timeouts.

panels.title: Days since last completed, by section
panels.description: Days since each maintenance checklist section was last marked completed. Rising values highlight overdue work.

panels.title: Failed or skipped in the last 90 days
panels.description: Maintenance log entries with a failed or skipped status over the last 90 days: work that still needs attention.

panels.title: Recent maintenance entries
panels.description: Most recent entries from the maintenance log, all statuses.
